title: Assessing the Morphological Changes of Residual Gadolinium-based Contrast Agents Found in Tissue via Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: The widespread concern among patients regarding the safety of gadolinium (Gd)-based contrast agents in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has driven ongoing debate and scrutiny, though extensive global research remains limited. The motivation stems from the fact that Gd-based contrast agents have been linked to nephrogenic systemic fibrosis (NSF), acute kidney injury and other adverse health conditions [1-4]. Such detrimental effects have been reported irrespective of the type of contrast agent used for imaging purposes (linear or macrocyclic, classified according to the molecular structure of the ligand used to bind the metal Gd3+) and in patients with normal or compromised renal function [1].
